text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 18 billion levs in the first half of March to 240 billion levs, Finance ministry figures showed. @

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev was dismissed because of lack of initiative and flexibility in the privatisation process and a lack of coordination with the supervisory board and the government, supervisory board chairman Yosif Iliev said.
-- Bulgaria should sell at least one state bank by end-May, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Bulgaria started distribution of 20 million Ecus of social aid granted by the European Union to poor Bulgarians. @

-- Bulgaria's deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov is expected to take part in discussions on rescheduling Bulgaria's debt to the G-24 countries at a meeting of the G-24 consultative group in Brussels on April 8 and 9.
-- The Sofia City Court is expected to rule within two weeks on an insolvency case against private Trade and Savings Bank filed by the Bulgarian National Bank, court officials said.
-- Germany's Foreign minister Klaus Kinkel is expected to arrive in Bulgaria and meet President Petar Stoyanov, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski and the Foreign minister Stoyan Stalev.
-- Bulgaria expects to receive some $100 million from the sale of a 60 percent stake in the Varna shipyard, shipyard officials said.
-- Bulgaria's biggest Confederation of Independent Trade Unions said some 85 percent of Bulgarian households can not meet even basic needs because of high prices of foods and energy.
-- Some 49 percent of Bulgarians would support the country's integration in the European Union if a referendum on the issue was held, a EU poll figures showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
